subject: Competitive bake-off recap: Redwood vs VendorX & VendorY
messages:

Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 5 Dec 2026 15:02:00 -0800
Subject: Competitive bake-off recap: Redwood vs VendorX & VendorY

Hi Samantha / Tom -

Thanks again for your time today. Quick recap from our discovery so we're all aligned on goals, pain points, and next steps for the bake-off. Please shout if anything below is off.

Key pain points you called out:
- P95 latency spikes (esp. during EOD workloads) causing slow UX and retries
- High unit cost on current provider when running at scale
- Lack of a private/VPC option for PHI-sensitive flows + needing key management controls
- Limited tracing / token-level cost visibility for debugging customer issues

Primary goals for this evaluation:
1) Consistent latency: target P95 < 300ms for 512-token requests in your EU region
2) Predictable unit economics: < $0.30 / 1k tokens for production traffic profile
3) Private deployment option (VPC or on-prem) with KMS/HSM integration
4) Strong observability (per-route breakdown, KV cache hit insights) and regression alerts

Decision criteria we agreed to measure:
- Latency: P50/P95/P99 under realistic traffic mix
- Throughput: sustained QPS (baseline + burst)
- Quality: response correctness on your 50 prompt eval set
- Cost: cost per 1M tokens at observed efficiency (batching/quant)
- Security/compliance: SOC2 + encryption at rest/in transit, audit logs

Quick vendor comparison (high level) - see attached bake-off matrix for details: redwood-bakeoff-matrix.xlsx
- Redwood: strong latency tuning, private deployment available, built-in tracing and rollout controls
- VendorX: lower up-front price but limited private deployment options, weaker tracing
- VendorY: good quality models but higher cost at scale and limited enterprise SLAs

Open questions / items we need from OmniHealth:
- Confirm the 50-prompt eval set (can you share as a CSV?)
- Preferred region(s) to run tests (you mentioned us-west + eu-west)
- Target traffic profile for throughput tests (baseline QPS and peak burst)

Proposed bake-off plan / timeline:
- Kickoff (technical): Mon 2026-12-07 - run through test harness and endpoints
- 48-hour automated run using your eval prompts + synthetic burst window
- Deliverables: latency/throughput report, quality eval, cost model, SOC2 evidence

Next steps (for this week):
- OmniHealth: share eval prompt CSV + target QPS by EOD Mon 12/07
- Redwood: provide test endpoints, SOC2 attestation, and bake-off matrix (attached)
- Schedule 30-min tech deep-dive (I've proposed slots Mon 12/07 10:00 or 14:00 PT)

Attachments: redwood-bakeoff-matrix.xlsx, redwood-architecture.png

Thanks - looking forward to running the tests and getting you concrete numbers.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Enterprise Solutions
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Competitive bake-off recap: Redwood vs VendorX & VendorY

Thanks Marissa - this is helpful and captures the discussion. A few clarifying Qs from our side:

1) For the SOC2 evidence, can you share the most recent report (redacted) and an inventory of controls that cover encryption/key management? Our security team will want to validate before we run any private deployment tests.

2) On the on-prem / private deployment option: is there a lightweight pilot we can run in our staging VPC (no PHI) to validate latency and KV/cache behavior before moving to any PHI workloads? Ideally something we can stand up in under a week.

3) Pricing: procurement asked for a two-sided guardrail - what's the expected cost range for the 48-hour bake-off (so they can log an initial estimate)?

We can share the 50-prompt CSV by Monday. For regions: please test us-west-2 and eu-west-1. Baseline QPS is 8rps, peak burst 40rps.

Appreciate the quick turnaround.

Samantha

Director, Product Operations

Date: Mon, 7 Dec 2026 08:12:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Competitive bake-off recap: Redwood vs VendorX & VendorY

Hi Samantha - thanks for the questions. Quick answers and next actions below.

1) SOC2: attached is our SOC2 Type II attestation (SOC2-Attestation.pdf). Redacted controls + summary included. We also support customer-managed KMS (AWS KMS/HSM) for private deployments - we'll provide an architecture diagram (attached: redwood-architecture.png).

2) Private/staging pilot: yes - we routinely run a lightweight staging pilot inside customer VPCs with no PHI. For your staging pilot we can deliver a Docker-based drop-in that runs in <24 hours with sample workloads. The pilot config will include:
- preconfigured test harness endpoints for load and latency capture
- KV cache enabled to mirror production usage
- metrics export to your CloudWatch / Datadog sandbox

3) Bake-off cost estimate: For the 48-hour run at baseline 8rps + 40rps peak burst, estimate is ~$450-$700 total for the test window (depends on batching & quantization settings). We'll aim to keep it at the lower end with aggressive batching and caching.

Proposed next steps:
- I've queued the SOC2 PDF and architecture PNG (attached).
- DocuSign link for our standard MSA/NDA (one-click sign for pilot): https://www.docusign.com/sign?xyz=abc123
- Can we kick off the staging pilot Mon 12/07 at 10:00 PT? We'll need your CI/CD point of contact and an IAM role for the VPC test account.

If that works I'll have our infra engineer (Aditya) own the pilot run and send test endpoints + a short README.

Onward -
Marissa
